title: A reduced Hopf core with nilpotent augmentation fibre
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. A commutative Hopf $k$-algebra here means a unital commutative $k$-algebra $A$ with $k$-algebra maps $\Delta_A:A\to A\otimes_k A$, $\epsilon_A:A\to k$, $S_A:A\to A$ such that $(\Delta_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\Delta_A)\Delta_A$, $(\epsilon_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\epsilon_A)\Delta_A=1_A$, and $\mu_A(S_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=\mu_A(1\otimes S_A)\Delta_A=\eta_A\epsilon_A$, under the usual tensor unit and associativity identifications; $\mu_A$ and $\eta_A$ are multiplication and unit. Tensor products are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. A Hopf homomorphism $u:P\to Q$ means a $k$-algebra homomorphism with $\Delta_Qu=(u\otimes u)\Delta_P$, $\epsilon_Qu=\epsilon_P$ and $S_Qu=uS_P$. Let $A$ be a commutative Hopf $k$-algebra finitely generated as a $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. There exists a $k$-subalgebra $C\subseteq A$ that is stable under $S_A$, whose comultiplication takes values in $C\otimes_k C$, and whose restricted structure maps make $C\hookrightarrow A$ a Hopf homomorphism. The algebra $C$ is finitely generated over $k$ and reduced (has no nonzero nilpotent element). Put $C^+=\ker(\epsilon_A|_C)$ and $D=A/(C^+A)$, where $C^+A$ is the ideal generated by $C^+$ in $A$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The counit induces $\bar\epsilon:D\to k$, and its ideal $\ker\bar\epsilon$ is nilpotent: $(\ker\bar\epsilon)^N=0$ for some integer $N\geq1$. In characteristic zero one can take $C=A$; in characteristic $p>0$ one can take $C=\{a^{p^r}:a\in A\}$ for some integer $r\geq1$.

source.place: Theorem 3.23, printed pp.70--71 (characteristic zero), Proposition 3.29, pp.72--73 (Frobenius image), and Theorem 3.31, p.74 (the kernel M of H to H-prime).

proof.text: A field is Noetherian: a nonzero ideal contains a unit, hence is the whole field, while the zero ideal is generated by the empty family. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to $k\to A$. Thus every ideal of $A$ is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Fix algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]; $m=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Proposition 3.29, p.73, finite generation of the nilradical; Stacks 00FN, algebra-lemma-Noetherian-permanence.

proof.text: Suppose first that $\operatorname{char}k=0$. If a nilpotent $b\in A$ were nonzero, its annihilator $J=\{a:ab=0\}$ would be a proper ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] take a maximal ideal $M\supseteq J$. Clause (1) of [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] gives a $k$-algebra map $g:A\to k$ with kernel $M$; its hypothesis requires finite generation, not reducedness. Apply [lem-sfb-hopf-nilpotent-rational-annihilator], using step 1, to obtain $t$ with $g(t)=1$ and $tb=0$. Then $t\in J\subseteq M=\ker g$, a contradiction. Hence $A$ is reduced. Take $C=A$. The identity inclusion is Hopf and $C^+A=\ker\epsilon_A$, since that kernel is already an ideal. The induced counit on $A/\ker\epsilon_A$ is injective by its kernel definition, so its augmentation ideal is zero; choose $N=1$. This proves every characteristic-zero clause.

source.place: Theorem 3.23, p.71; rational-point local argument made explicit using the existing Cartier theorem and Nullstellensatz.

proof.text: Now suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, with $p$ prime. Let $J$ be the nilradical, the ideal of nilpotent elements. It is an ideal: products with arbitrary elements remain nilpotent, and the binomial expansion shows that $u^a=v^b=0$ implies $(u+v)^{a+b}=0$. By step 1 choose generators $z_1,\ldots,z_s$ and exponents $e_i\geq1$ with $z_i^{e_i}=0$. For $n=1+\sum_i(e_i-1)$, each degree-$n$ monomial in the $z_i$ contains some $z_i^{e_i}$; expanding products gives $J^n=0$. Choose $r\geq1$ with $q=p^r\geq n$. Every $z\in J$ then has $z^q=0$. For $J=0$ the empty generating family gives $n=1$.

source.place: Proposition 3.29, p.73: the uniform nilpotence exponent, expanded by the finite-generator monomial argument.

proof.text: By [def-weil-ring-frobenius], $F^r:a\mapsto a^q$ is a ring homomorphism. Every $\lambda\in k$ has a $q$th root, since $T^q-\lambda$ has a root by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Therefore its image $C=\{a^q:a\in A\}$ is a $k$-subalgebra: $a^q+b^q=(a+b)^q$, $a^qb^q=(ab)^q$, and $\lambda a^q=(ca)^q$ for $c^q=\lambda$. Moreover $C=k[x_1^q,\ldots,x_m^q]$: for $a=P(x_1,\ldots,x_m)$, raising its finite polynomial expression to $q$ gives a polynomial in $x_i^q$ with coefficients in $k$; the reverse inclusion follows from the subalgebra property. Thus $C$ is finitely generated. If $c=a^q\in C$ is nilpotent, then $a$ is nilpotent, hence belongs to $J$ and $a^q=0$ by step 3. Thus $C$ is reduced.

source.place: Proposition 3.29, pp.72--73: power image, perfection and reducedness; polynomial generators written explicitly.

proof.text: The inclusion $C\hookrightarrow A$ induces injections on every finite tensor power over $k$: extend a $k$-basis of $C$ to one of $A$ and use the tensor bases. If $\Delta_A(a)=\sum_i u_i\otimes v_i$, then [def-weil-ring-frobenius] in the commutative ring $A\otimes_k A$ gives $\Delta_A(a^q)=\sum_i u_i^q\otimes v_i^q$, which lies in the injected $C\otimes_k C$. Also $S_A(a^q)=S_A(a)^q\in C$. Define $\Delta_C$ by this unique factorization, and restrict $S_A$ and $\epsilon_A$ to $C$. They are $k$-algebra maps because their composites with the injective inclusions are such maps. The two coassociativity composites become those for $A$ after injection into $A^{\otimes3}$, so they agree. Both counit identities become the identity of $C$ after injection into $A$. Likewise both antipode composites become $\eta_A\epsilon_A|_C$ in $A$, hence equal $\eta_C\epsilon_C$ in $C$. Thus these maps make $C$ Hopf and its inclusion a Hopf homomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 3.29, pp.72--73, and Proposition 3.9, p.67: the restricted Hopf structure is verified directly.

proof.text: Put $I=\ker\epsilon_A$ and $y_i=x_i-\epsilon_A(x_i)$. Then $I=(y_1,\ldots,y_m)$: for each polynomial $P$, the difference $P(x)-P(\epsilon_A(x))$ belongs to this ideal, by expanding one monomial at a time, and the reverse inclusion follows by applying $\epsilon_A$. Let $K=C^+A$. Since $\epsilon_A(C^+)=0$, $K\subseteq I$ and the quotient counit $\bar\epsilon:A/K\to k$ is well defined. Its kernel is exactly the ideal of classes of $I$, hence is generated by the classes $\bar y_i$. Each $y_i^q\in C$ and $\epsilon_A(y_i^q)=0$, so $y_i^q\in C^+$ and $\bar y_i^q=0$. Set $N=1+m(q-1)$. Every degree-$N$ monomial in these $m$ generators contains a $q$th power, hence is zero. Expanding products gives $(\ker\bar\epsilon)^N=0$. If $m=0$, the kernel is zero and $N=1$. Together with steps 4--5 this proves all positive-characteristic clauses.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, p.74, nilpotence of the augmentation ideal of O(M); the generator calculation omitted there is written out.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 3.23, Proposition 3.29 and the kernel in Theorem 3.31, pp.71--74; explicit polynomial, tensor-injection and nilpotent-fibre calculations; characteristic-zero local input taken from its existing project theorem.

The item statement is unchanged. New node: true. It is exactly the public, sorry-free theorem HopfAlgebra.exists_apply_eq_one_mul_eq_zero_of_isNilpotent (Cartier.lean:787-799; variables Field/CommRing/HopfAlgebra/CharZero/IsNoetherianRing). Small cases: k[t]/(t^p) in char p fails the conclusion, so char 0 is essential. Every object is introduced in the node. It does not restate a clause of the item: it is local, holds for Noetherian A over any char-0 field and says nothing about global reducedness or quotients. Not a duplicate: lem-ag-cartier-reduced is stored only for subgroups of GL(V) over Q̄_ℓ, and lem-sfb-affine-group-frobenius-smooth-image cites this item, so citing it would make a cycle. Steps: (1) the finite-type-Noetherian leaf and generators are correct. (2) Ann(b) is proper, sits in a maximal ideal, and Nullstellensatz clause (1) needs only finite type, giving g with kernel M; the new node gives t, a contradiction; with C=A the fibre ideal is 0 and N=1. (3) The nilradical is finitely generated with J^n=0, n=1+Σ(e_i−1), by pigeonhole. (4) A^q is a k-subalgebra using q-th roots in k and equals k[x_i^q]; it is reduced by step 3. (5) Δ(a^q)=Σu_i^q⊗v_i^q by Frobenius in A⊗A, S is multiplicative, and all Hopf identities are checked after the injective tensor inclusions. (6) ker ε=(y_i), ȳ_i^q=0 and N=1+m(q−1). The edge cases m=0, J=0, k[t], G_m and k[t]/(t^{p^e}) are consistent. No cycle. No SGA. Accepted tool use: lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing clause (1) as a generic tool, following the precedent of other sfb nodes. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_reduced_core_nilpotent_fibre (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CommRing A] [HopfAlgebra k A] (hA : (algebraMap k A).FiniteType) : ∃ C : Subalgebra k A, (algebraMap k C).FiniteType ∧ IsReduced C ∧ (∃ hC : HopfAlgebra k C, hC.toBialgebra.toAlgebra = (inferInstance : Algebra k C) ∧ ∃ i : @BialgHom k C A _ _ hC.toBialgebra.toAlgebra _ _ hC.toBialgebra.toCoalgebra.toCoalgebraStruct _, (∀ c : C, i c = (c : A)) ∧ ∀ c : C, i (@antipode k C _ _ hC.toHopfAlgebraStruct c) = antipode k (i c)) ∧ (∃ εbar : (A ⧸ Ideal.span {a : A | a ∈ C ∧ Bialgebra.counitAlgHom k A a = 0}) →ₐ[k] k, εbar.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ k (Ideal.span {a : A | a ∈ C ∧ Bialgebra.counitAlgHom k A a = 0})) = Bialgebra.counitAlgHom k A ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N ∧ RingHom.ker εbar ^ N = ⊥) ∧ (CharZero k → C = ⊤) ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → (p : k) = 0 → ∃ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r ∧ (C : Set A) = Set.range (fun a : A ↦ a ^ (p ^ r))
